findings.title: Physical delete is non-recoverable
findings.description: The mapped SQL issues a hard DELETE on COMPANY with no soft-delete or audit hook; an accidental or buggy invocation permanently removes the matching row.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether logical deletion or an audit record is required; otherwise enforce caller-side authorization and logging.

findings.title: Null parameters yield a silent no-op
findings.description: A null id or companyState binds to `= NULL` predicates that match no rows, so the DELETE silently deletes nothing without error.
findings.recommendation: Validate id and companyState are non-null before invoking the mapper, or add a guard precondition.

findings.title: Affected-row scope depends on ID uniqueness
findings.description: The number of deleted rows depends on the uniqueness of COMPANY.ID; if ID is not unique, multiple rows may be deleted.
findings.recommendation: Confirm ID is uniquely constrained on COMPANY and check the affected-row count before commit.
